memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time Joshua went and destroyed the Anakites from the hill country: from Hebron, Debir and Anab, from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua totally destroyed them and their towns. No Anakites were left in Israelite territory; only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did any survive - Josh 11:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Anakites were the giants — the very people whose size had terrified the twelve spies a generation earlier. Back then, ten of the spies had looked at these towering men and said, "We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes" (Num 13:33). Their fear of the Anakites had cost that whole generation the Promised Land.

Now, years later, here is Joshua cutting the giants down. The very fear that once paralysed Israel is met and overcome. What a mercy of God, that the thing the parents fled from, the children were enabled to face. God did not remove the giants; He gave His people the strength to face them at the right time.

Perhaps you are carrying a fear you inherited or one that has loomed over you for years — a giant you have long believed you could never overcome. This chapter whispers hope. The giants that once seemed unbeatable fall when God's people go forward in His strength rather than shrinking back in their own. The battle was still the Lord's (1 Sam 17:47), just as David would later remember when he faced a giant of his own. And our greatest giants — sin, fear, even death — have already been faced and defeated by Christ (1 Cor 15:57). The giant that terrified one generation was cut down in the next; the giants that terrify us are already conquered in Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "giant" have you long believed you could never overcome?
- How does it help to know God gives strength to face fears in His timing?
- Which of your giants has Christ already defeated on your behalf?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, the giants in my life feel too big for me. Thank You that in Christ even sin and death are already defeated. Give me courage to go forward in Your strength. Amen.
